summary: EfficientNet-B5 Phase 2 on crops dataset, second attempt. lr=5e-5 (down from 1.5e-4 in b5_crop_v1/phase2), backbone-lr-scale=0.33, wd=0.01, bs=12, grad-accum-steps=2, 30 epochs. Loaded phase1 checkpoint. Best overall accuracy 75.51% at epoch 3 — +1.01pp vs b5_crop_v1/phase2 (74.50%). Same plateau pattern: peaked at ep3, oscillated 74.7-75.5% for remaining 27 epochs with no further improvement. val_loss climbed from 0.882 to 1.039 (slower than v1's 0.886→1.281, but same direction). Lower lr reduced calibration damage but did not resolve the fundamental plateau.

comparison.vs_b5_crop_v1_phase2: +1.01pp overall (75.51% vs 74.50%). Lower lr modestly improved all per-task results and significantly reduced val_loss divergence (1.039 vs 1.281 at ep30). But the plateau pattern is identical — peaked early, no improvement after.
comparison.vs_b5_crop_v1_phase1: Phase 1 task regression persists: stories 76.49%→73.52% (-2.97pp), roof_type 67.22%→63.61% (-3.61pp), primary_cladding 77.46%→74.62% (-2.84pp). Less severe than v1/phase2 but still real. Backbone interference is still happening.
comparison.vs_resnet50_phase2: arch_style 73.62% vs 70.76% ResNet50 (+2.86pp). B5+crops still wins on the new phase2 tasks despite the plateau.

learnings: Lower lr (5e-5 vs 1.5e-4) is better — less val_loss divergence, slightly higher peak accuracy — but does not fix the root cause.

Root cause confirmed: the plateau is not an lr problem. The backbone is simultaneously being pulled by 7 task heads from two phases with conflicting gradient signals. New heads (arch_style, building_form) are at random init while phase1 heads are fully converged — the optimizer cannot satisfy both simultaneously.
Two lr experiments (1.5e-4 and 5e-5) both peaked at ep1-3 and plateaued. Further lr reduction is unlikely to help — the gradient conflict is structural.

Next required experiment: --freeze-phase1-heads. This locks phase1 head weights so only the backbone and new heads receive updates. Expected outcome: phase1 task accuracy holds at phase1 levels (frozen heads = no regression), new heads converge properly over 10-15 epochs.
After freeze warmup (e.g. 15 epochs), optionally unfreeze all heads with a very low lr (1e-5) for joint fine-tuning.
next_steps: b5_crop_v3/phase2: --freeze-phase1-heads, lr=1e-4 (new heads need reasonable lr to converge from random init), backbone-lr-scale=0.1 (backbone at 1e-5, very conservative).
Success criterion: phase1 tasks (stories, cladding, roof_type) should hold within 1pp of phase1 baseline. arch_style should reach ≥75% by ep15.
If freeze run succeeds, consider a second stage: resume from b5_crop_v3 best checkpoint, unfreeze all heads, lr=1e-5 across the board for final joint polish.
